text: Singapore remains biggest investor in HCM City with $25.28 billion
Cumulatively, Singapore had invested in 2,815 projects in Ho Chi Minh City as of the end of September 2026, with total registered capital exceeding $25.28 billion.
The figures reflect Singaporean investors' confidence in the southern city's growth potential and offer opportunities for expanded cooperation in high technology, infrastructure and logistics.

Speaking at the recent Ho Chi Minh City-Singapore Investment Promotion Conference, Mr. Nguyen Loc Ha, Standing Vice Chairman of the municipal People's Committee, said the two countries' elevation of bilateral ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in March 2025 had created a favourable framework for practical and effective cooperation.
Mr. Pang Te Cheng, Singapore's Consul General in Ho Chi Minh City, said bilateral trade reached S$42.8 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up nearly 47% year-on-year.
He noted that relations between the two countries were entering a new phase following the partnership upgrade.
The conference highlighted fresh opportunities for investment and cooperation, reaffirming Singapore's position as a leading investor in Ho Chi Minh City.
With strong commitments from both sides and support from financial institutions such as UOB, the city aims to attract further investment to promote sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
